entities.name: Accenture — Disability Inclusion
entities.description: Global professional services company with comprehensive disability inclusion and hiring program, supporting neurodivergent and disabled employees across multiple markets.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected because Accenture demonstrates sustained commitment to inclusive employment at scale, employing thousands of people with disabilities and actively building accessible technology solutions.
entities.contributionSummary: Operates global disability hiring programs, provides workplace accommodations and assistive technology, and develops inclusive business practices. Employs over 3% of workforce with disabilities and partners on accessibility solutions.
entities.insights: Notable for demonstrating that disability inclusion is compatible with high-performance technical work and for embedding accessibility into product design across enterprise consulting.

evidence.description: Official program description of Accenture's comprehensive approach to recruiting, retaining and developing employees with disabilities.
Describes Accenture's commitment to accessibility in technology products and services.

entities.name: Microsoft — Disability Hiring Initiative
entities.description: Technology giant with formal disability hiring program and accessibility research division, focusing on employment pathways and assistive technology innovation.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating that technology sector participation is achievable for disabled professionals and for active research into accessibility solutions that benefit broader society.
entities.contributionSummary: Operates a formal autism hiring program and disability hiring initiatives. Conducts research in assistive technology and collaborates with disability organizations on product accessibility.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that specific neurodiversity-focused hiring (e.g., autism hiring) can create meaningful employment pathways while generating innovation benefits for the broader organization.

evidence.description: Overview of Microsoft's formal disability and neurodiversity hiring programs.
Research group focused on developing technologies that enable people with disabilities.

entities.name: Leonard Cheshire Disability
entities.description: UK-based disability organisation operating independent living schemes, employment programmes, and supporting disabled people across multiple life domains.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating holistic support for disabled people including employment, housing and community participation, with evidence-based programmes.
entities.contributionSummary: Operates residential and support services, employment training programmes, and advocacy work. Supports disabled people to live independently and participate in society.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that meaningful contribution requires integrated support across employment, housing, and community life—not employment alone.

evidence.description: Organisation homepage with overview of services and programmes.
Details of employment training and support programmes.

entities.name: Sense — Deaf-Blind Organisation
entities.description: UK-based organisation supporting deaf-blind and multi-sensory disabled people, providing specialist services including communication support and specialist advice.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating specialised support for complex disabilities and for leading voice in inclusive communication and accessibility innovation.
entities.contributionSummary: Provides communication support, residential services, advocacy for deaf-blind people, and expertise in accessible technology design.
entities.insights: Shows that meaningful inclusion sometimes requires specialized expertise and support, and that organizations led by disabled people's voices develop more effective solutions.

evidence.description: Specialist communication resources and support for deaf-blind people.

entities.name: Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB)
entities.description: UK-based charity supporting blind and partially sighted people through employment services, education, technology innovation, and advocacy.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for long-standing leadership in accessibility innovation, employment training, and advancing technology standards that benefit all users.
entities.contributionSummary: Operates employment training services, develops accessible technology solutions, provides educational resources, and leads advocacy for accessibility standards.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that accessibility innovation benefits broader society—technologies designed for blind users often improve usability for all.

evidence.description: Organisation homepage with services and programmes overview.

entities.name: Autistica
entities.description: UK-based research and evidence organisation led by and for autistic people, investigating how to improve health, wellbeing, and independence.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating that disabled people's leadership in research produces more relevant, applicable insights and for building evidence base for effective inclusion.
entities.contributionSummary: Conducts research led by autistic people, provides evidence on effective workplace accommodations and education approaches, and advocates for autistic-led policy.
entities.insights: Shows the value of centering disabled people's knowledge and lived experience in research and policymaking rather than treating them as subjects of study.

evidence.description: Portfolio of research projects led by autistic researchers.

entities.name: The Valuable 500
entities.description: Global movement of business leaders committed to disability inclusion in the workplace, with participating companies representing over $3 trillion in annual revenue.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for mobilising corporate leadership around disability inclusion and demonstrating business case for diversity at scale.
entities.contributionSummary: Convenes 500+ business leaders across sectors and geographies to advance disability inclusion in workforce, procurement, and products. Shares best practices and holds members accountable.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that disability inclusion is increasingly recognized as a business imperative by mainstream corporate leadership, not just a social responsibility.

entities.name: Remploy — Supported Employment
entities.description: UK provider of employment services and supported employment programmes specifically designed to help disabled people secure and maintain work.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating practical supported employment models that enable disabled people to compete in open labour market with appropriate support.
entities.contributionSummary: Provides job matching, workplace support, skills training, and ongoing employment coaching for disabled people. Works with employers to create sustainable inclusive workplaces.
entities.insights: Shows that high-quality employment support enables disabled people to contribute in competitive employment, not just segregated or subsidised work.

entities.name: Inclusive Arts Collective
entities.description: Global movement supporting disabled artists and creatives, demonstrating artistic contribution, leadership, and cultural participation.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for highlighting artistic and cultural contribution of disabled people and challenging stereotypes of disability as non-creative.
entities.contributionSummary: Supports disabled artists in creating and exhibiting work, advocates for disability representation in arts, and builds platforms for disabled creative leadership.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that cultural participation and artistic contribution are essential dimensions of full community participation, not optional extras.

evidence.description: Directory and network of inclusive arts initiatives globally.

entities.name: International Paralympic Committee
entities.description: Global governance body for Paralympic movement, demonstrating athletic excellence, international competition, and sports participation by disabled athletes.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for establishing competitive sports pathways that demonstrate excellence and capability of disabled athletes at world-class level.
entities.contributionSummary: Organizes Paralympic Games, sets global standards for disability sports, supports national paralympic committees, and advocates for athlete rights and inclusion.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that disabled people's athletic excellence is comparable to non-disabled athletes and that competitive sport is a legitimate pathway for contribution and achievement.

entities.name: EmpleYarTech
entities.description: Latin American platform connecting disabled people with technology sector opportunities through training, mentorship, and job placement.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for demonstrating technology sector inclusion in emerging economy context and for developing innovative training pathways for disabled professionals.
entities.contributionSummary: Provides technology skills training, mentorship from tech professionals, and employment pathways in growing tech sector across Latin America.
entities.insights: Shows that inclusive employment in high-growth sectors like technology is achievable globally, not only in wealthy economies, with appropriate support structures.
perspectives: Disabled job seekers in emerging markets

entities.name: Scope — Cerebral Palsy Equality
entities.description: UK equality and rights organisation for disabled people, specifically those with cerebral palsy and other physical disabilities, campaigning for equality and inclusion.
entities.selectionRationale: Selected for disability rights leadership and for advocating systemic changes needed for inclusion beyond individual service provision.
entities.contributionSummary: Runs campaigns for disability equality, provides advocacy and advice services, and conducts research on barriers to disabled people's participation and employment.
entities.insights: Demonstrates that addressing disabled people's contribution requires systemic change and advocacy, not only individual support services.

evidence.description: Ongoing policy and systemic change campaigns.
